subject: Dedicated capacity — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and the follow-ups we discussed so we stay aligned as you evaluate a Dedicated capacity reservation with Redwood: 

High-level summary from call:
- Estimated monthly token volume: ~1.0–1.4B tokens/month (you said traffic is spiky with ~40M tokens/day peak)
- Primary workload: customer-facing chat and multi-turn system prompts, typical input sequences ~256 tokens, output ~256 tokens (average turn ~500 tokens)
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a goal of ~$35–$45 per 1M tokens (equivalent to a monthly budget range of ~$30k–$45k for the above volume)
- Latency/throughput targets: p50 latency target ~<200ms for short-turn replies; throughput target ~200–400 tokens/sec sustained across the pool

Follow-ups / clarifying questions (so we can provide an apples-to-apples Dedicated estimate):
1) Preferred GPU family: do you have a hard requirement for H100 or is A100 acceptable? H100 gives better throughput on larger models, A100 can be more cost-efficient for some quantized stacks.
2) Peak concurrent sessions / QPS estimate (or example traffic curve). This helps size reserved vGPU count.
3) Any strict latency SLOs (p95) that we should design to meet?
4) Are you planning single-model serving or multi-model variants (e.g., a larger model for long responses + a smaller model fallback)?

Attached is a quick estimate worksheet (RDW-Dedicated-Estimate-20270405.xlsx) with a few sizing options: 2x H100, 4x H100, and 8x A100 pools and the rough $/1M token math.

Proposed next steps:
- If you can confirm the GPU preference and a more precise peak concurrency number, I’ll loop in Marcus (performance/engineering) and Vanessa (contracts) and share a tailored committed-capacity quote.
- Optional tech deep-dive: Marcus can run a quick perf simulation with your sample payload and give a throughput/latency estimate for each GPU config. Would next Wed (Apr 7) or Thu (Apr 8) work?

Thanks — I’ll hold Monday/Tuesday for follow-up.

Best,
Marissa

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few answers below:

- Monthly tokens: our conservative estimate is ~1.2B tokens/month with occasional +/- 20% seasonality.
- Budget: headroom for committed spend around $30k–$45k/month. We were hoping to see unit economics in the ~$35–$45 per 1M tokens range — that would put us in the acceptable band.
- GPU preference: we would prefer H100 if you recommend it for our workload (low-latency chat + multi-turn).
- Peak concurrency: during business hours we expect ~600 concurrent chat sessions, average turnaround ~1–2 messages per second per session during peaks — rough QPS ~800–1,200 requests/sec.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 200ms; p95 < 800ms would be ideal.
- Models: single production model to start (a 34B/70B class), with a plan for a smaller fallback model in future (could be a config change, not immediate).

We’re happy to do the tech deep-dive. Thu Apr 8 10:00am PT works for Alex + our infra lead. Please include Marcus for perf sims.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chen | Product Lead, AI Experiences
alex.chen@acme.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-03T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — post-call recap & next steps

Perfect — thanks for the details, Alex. Quick readout on sizing and what we'll run in the deep-dive: 

Sizing baseline (back-of-envelope):
- Workload assumptions: avg request ~500 tokens, 1.2B tokens/month -> ~2.4M requests/month (~80k requests/day)
- Throughput target: to meet p50 <200ms and sustain ~1,000 req/sec peak with batching, we'd recommend starting with a 4x H100 reserved pool.
  - 4x H100 (shared across routing) gives headroom for batching and maintains low single-request latency for small batches.
  - If you need higher concurrency (>=1,500 req/sec peak), we should target 6x–8x H100.
- A100 option: 8x A100 is cost-competitive but typically higher latency for the same throughput compared to H100 for 70B-class models. Good fallback if budget is tighter.

Unit economics examples (very rough):
- 4x H100 reserved: estimated committed cost ~$38k/month -> implied ~$32–$38 per 1M tokens depending on utilization/batching gains.
- 8x A100 reserved: estimated committed cost ~$29k/month -> implied ~$24–$32 per 1M tokens (but higher tail latencies).

What Marcus will do on the deep-dive:
- Run perf sims with a 70B-like model profile using your sample prompts (we'll need one or two representative prompts you can share).
- Produce p50/p95 latency estimates and tokens/sec for 2/4/6 H100 and 4/8 A100 configs.
- Confirm whether KV-cache persistence or prefix caching can improve unit economics for multi-turn chat.

Next steps:
1) Confirm deep-dive Thu Apr 8 10:00am PT — Marcus will invite a join link.
2) Alex: if you can share 2 sample prompts and a short traffic curve (CSV or bullet points) before the call, Marcus can run targeted sims.
3) After the deep-dive we’ll share a tailored committed-capacity quote (including uplift for burst capacity and optional SLA).

On pricing: I included three pricing bands in the attached estimate to show tradeoffs. We can tighten those numbers after Marcus' sims.

Thanks — looping Marcus & Vanessa into this thread to coordinate.

Best,
Marissa
